title: Devotion to the form and the formless

verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचएवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते । येचाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमाः ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: Those devotees who worship You with constant devotion, and those who worship the imperishable, unmanifest reality, who among them are the most accomplished in yoga?
verses.angle: Arjuna asks which of two types of devotees are better yogis
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Krishna has just shown Arjuna his universal form. Now, before the war resumes, Arjuna asks a sharp question about the two paths of worship.

body.text: Arjuna says: Those devotees who worship You with constant devotion, and those who worship the imperishable, unmanifest reality, who among them are the most accomplished in yoga? Arjuna asks who are the best yogis: those who worship Krishna personally, or those who worship the unmanifest, formless absolute. Krishna answers that those who worship him with unwavering devotion and supreme trust are the highest yogis.

verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते । श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः ॥
verses.tr: Those who focus their mind on me, worship me with unwavering devotion, and are filled with supreme trust are, in my view, the highest yogis.
verses.angle: Highest yogis are those who fix their mind on Him
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna answers by naming the highest yogis, and He defines them by their steady focus and complete trust.

body.text: Those who focus their mind on me, worship me with unwavering devotion, and are filled with supreme trust are, in my view, the highest yogis. Krishna calls those who fix their mind on Him with supreme trust the highest yogis, and He uses the word nityayuktah, always united, to show that steady focus is the mark of the best. Krishna then names those who worship the unmanifest, the eternal, and the imperishable, restraining the senses to reach Him alone.

verses.sa: ये त्वक्षरमनिर्देश्यमव्यक्तं पर्युपासते । सर्वत्रगमचिन्त्यं च कूटस्थमचलं ध्रुवम् ॥
verses.tr: Those who worship the unchanging, the indefinable, the unmanifest, the all-pervading, the unthinkable, the unmoving, the eternal, the imperishable, restraining the senses, reach Me alone.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: This verse answers the question of who is the best devotee. Listen for the qualities Krishna gives to those who worship the formless.

body.text: Those who worship the unchanging, the indefinable, the unmanifest, the all-pervading, the unthinkable, the unmoving, the eternal, the imperishable, restraining the senses, reach Me alone. Notice the word acintyam, unthinkable. The divine is not an object the mind can picture, and yet those who worship this unthinkable reality with controlled senses reach Krishna. Krishna then says that those who restrain the senses and remain even-minded and delight in the welfare of all beings reach him alone.

verses.sa: संनियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः । ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥
verses.tr: Those who restrain the senses, remain even-minded everywhere, and delight in the welfare of all beings reach me alone.
verses.angle: sarvabhutahite ratah, the welfare of all beings
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Right before this verse, Krishna described the highest kind of worshipper. Now he turns to the shape of that worship.

body.text: Those who restrain the senses, remain even-minded everywhere, and delight in the welfare of all beings reach me alone. The key phrase here is sarvabhutahite ratah, delighting in the welfare of all beings. This means devotion is an active wish for the good of every living thing. Sanjaya says that for those who worship the unmanifest, the path is even harder and full of struggle.

verses.tr: For those whose minds cling to the unmanifest, the struggle is greater. The unmanifest path is hard to reach for embodied beings.
verses.angle: Clinging to the unmanifest brings greater struggle
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen closely to the word that tells us why the unmanifest path is so difficult, and why embodied beings find it hard.

body.text: For those whose minds cling to the unmanifest, the struggle is greater. The unmanifest path is hard to reach for embodied beings. Krishna warns that minds set on the unmanifest face more struggle, since embodied people find that path hard. Krishna now turns to the easier path of single-pointed devotion to a personal form.

verses.sa: ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः । अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते ॥
verses.tr: But those who surrender all actions to Me, take Me as their highest aim, and worship Me with single-pointed devotion, meditating on Me alone.
verses.angle: Total devotion turns every action into worship.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just said the unmanifest path is hard for those in a body. Now he names a different way, open to anyone.

body.text: But those who surrender all actions to Me, take Me as their highest aim, and worship Me with single-pointed devotion, meditating on Me alone. After saying the unmanifest is hard, Krishna names a path where a devotee places every single action at his feet and holds him as the highest aim. Krishna then says he quickly lifts those who follow this path out of the ocean of mortal existence, O Partha.

verses.sa: तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् । भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् ॥
verses.tr: I quickly become the one who lifts those whose minds are fixed on me from the ocean of mortal existence, O Partha.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna answers the devotee's deepest fear of being trapped in endless mortality with a promise to rescue them. Listen for the speed of his rescue.

body.text: I quickly become the one who lifts those whose minds are fixed on me from the ocean of mortal existence, O Partha. The word nacirata means not after long. Krishna does not promise rescue after many lifetimes, but very soon for those who fix their minds on him. Krishna then tells Arjuna to fix his mind on him alone and live in him beyond doubt.

verses.sa: मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय । निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः ॥
verses.tr: Fix your mind on me alone. Place your discerning mind in me, and you will live in me beyond doubt.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just promised to lift his devotees from the ocean of birth and death. Now he tells Arjuna the exact method to receive that rescue.

body.text: Fix your mind on me alone. Place your discerning mind in me, and you will live in me beyond doubt. The word buddhi means the discerning mind, and Krishna asks Arjuna to fix both his ordinary mind and his discerning mind on him. Krishna offers a backup plan: if the mind cannot rest on him, Arjuna should seek him through the practice of yoga.

verses.sa: अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम् । अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनञ्जय ॥
verses.tr: If you cannot steadily fix your mind on me, then, Dhananjaya, seek me through practice yoga.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna is still frozen, so Krishna offers a gentler rung if steady devotion feels too hard.

body.text: If you cannot steadily fix your mind on me, then, Dhananjaya, seek me through practice yoga. Practice yoga, repeated practice, is Krishna's fallback if you cannot hold your mind on him. If even practice feels too hard, Krishna offers a final, gentler path to reach him.

verses.sa: अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव । मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन् सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि ॥
verses.tr: If you are unable even to practice, then be devoted to working for Me. By doing actions for My sake, you will attain perfection.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen for one word that changes the nature of any action. Krishna lowers the bar for Arjuna again.

body.text: If you are unable even to practice, then be devoted to working for Me. By doing actions for My sake, you will attain perfection. Listen for madartham, for My sake. Krishna does not ask Arjuna to stop working or to meditate perfectly. He asks him to keep doing actions, but to do them for Krishna's sake. The work itself becomes the offering, and the offering itself becomes the path to perfection. If even this is too much, Krishna says, then simply renounce the fruits of your actions.

verses.sa: अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः । सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान् ॥
verses.tr: If you still cannot do even this while taking refuge in my yoga, then, self-controlled, renounce all fruits of action.
verses.angle: Renounce the fruit of action with a controlled mind
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has already offered the path of devotion and steady practice. Now he offers one last, simpler way. Listen to the final step down.

body.text: If you still cannot do even this while taking refuge in my yoga, then, self-controlled, renounce all fruits of action. The word yata-atman means a controlled self, and Krishna tells Arjuna to do exactly that: keep the mind steady and renounce the fruit of action. Krishna then says that knowledge is better than practice, leading to the next verse.

verses.tr: Knowledge is better than practice; meditation is better than knowledge. Renouncing the fruits of action is better than meditation, and peace follows at once from renunciation.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues by ranking the steps of the path, showing where the real release begins.

body.text: Knowledge is better than practice; meditation is better than knowledge. Renouncing the fruits of action is better than meditation, and peace follows at once from renunciation. The verse moves from meditation to a higher step, karma-phala-tyaga, renouncing the fruits of action. This letting go of personal reward is the exact moment peace arrives. Krishna now describes the person who has reached this state, one free from ego and equal in pleasure and pain.

verses.sa: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च । निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी ॥
verses.tr: One who hates no being, is friendly and compassionate, free from possessiveness and ego, equal in pleasure and pain, and forgiving.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna outlines the traits of a devotee who is dear to him. Listen for how he describes the absence of inner conflict.

body.text: One who hates no being, is friendly and compassionate, free from possessiveness and ego, equal in pleasure and pain, and forgiving. Krishna pairs two absences: without possessiveness and without ego. The devotee does not cling to possessions and does not claim the self, which leaves no room for inner conflict. Krishna then adds that this devotee remains equal in pain and pleasure, steady through all conditions.

verses.sa: सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः । मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥
verses.tr: The devoted yogi is always content, self-controlled, and steady in resolve. One whose mind and discerning mind are offered to Me is dear to Me.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna describes the one who is dear to Him by listing his inner qualities. Listen for the one who is steady.

body.text: The devoted yogi is always content, self-controlled, and steady in resolve. One whose mind and discerning mind are offered to Me is dear to Me. The verse ends with a direct statement: the devotee whose mind and intellect are offered to Me is dear to Me. The reward for all this self-control and resolve is simply being dear to Him. Krishna then adds another trait, that of one who is free from envy and fear.
